question: Who among the following Muslim leaders of British India joined the All - India Muslim League in 1913?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Muhammad Ali Jinnah**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Muhammad Ali Jinnah

 
 
• **Muhammad Ali Jinnah** joined the All-India Muslim League in **1913**.
 
• Jinnah was initially a member of the Indian National Congress and was known as a prominent leader advocating Hindu-Muslim unity.
 
• He joined the Muslim League to work towards securing political rights for Muslims within the framework of Indian self-governance.
 
• Jinnah later became the most influential leader of the Muslim League and played a pivotal role in the creation of Pakistan.
 
• His entry into the Muslim League marked a significant shift in the party's direction, as he brought a more moderate and inclusive approach.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Maulana Shaukat Ali:**

 
 
• Maulana Shaukat Ali was a prominent Muslim leader and a key figure in the **Khilafat Movement**.
 
• He was not associated with the All-India Muslim League in 1913.
 
• Along with his brother Maulana Muhammad Ali, he focused on uniting Indian Muslims against British policies affecting the Ottoman Caliphate.
 
• His political activities were more aligned with the Indian National Congress during this period.
 
• He did not join the Muslim League until much later, and his primary focus remained on the Khilafat Movement.
 
 
 
• **Maulana Abul Kalam Azad:**
 
 
• Maulana Abul Kalam Azad was a prominent leader of the **Indian National Congress** and a staunch advocate of Hindu-Muslim unity.
 
• He did not join the All-India Muslim League in 1913 or at any other time.
 
• Azad was a strong critic of the Muslim League's demand for Pakistan and remained committed to a united India.
 
• He served as the President of the Indian National Congress and played a significant role in India's independence movement.
 
• His political ideology was rooted in secularism and nationalism, which kept him away from the Muslim League.
 
 
 
• **Hakim Ajmal Khan:**
 
 
• Hakim Ajmal Khan was a renowned physician, educationalist, and nationalist leader.
 
• He was associated with the **Indian National Congress** and the **Khilafat Movement** but did not join the All-India Muslim League in 1913.
 
• Khan was a strong advocate of Hindu-Muslim unity and worked closely with leaders like Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• He focused on promoting education and healthcare, founding institutions like the **Jamia Millia Islamia**.
 
• His political activities were aligned with the Congress, and he did not associate with the Muslim League during this period.
